nodes.title: Release 16 (e807f07, integration 24) replaced production on 2026-11-10 on the owner's word that nobody is using it; production is the build the owner tests, and no staging app is created (the owner offered $40-50 a month for one; main declined). The 16 pending production migrations (031, 034-047, 050) were applied through the Neon connector, chosen by the owner over reading the app's secret: backup branch pre-release-e807f07 (no compute) first, a rehearsal of all 49 statements on branch rehearse-release-e807f07, then one all-or-nothing transaction on main (project taxila-us), with schema_migrations rows written as scripts/migrate-core.mjs writes them; verified 46 rows. release.mjs ran with --migrate skip and --force (the X37 evening freeze protects lessons in progress; there are none). Why: the release had waited since director16 on a Neon key the owner did not want to hand over; the connector needs no key in the repo or the chat. Reverse if: a real family starts using production (then: staging app via scripts/staging.mjs before any further release, the freeze is honoured again, and migrations go through scripts/migrate.mjs with a key in the secret store); or a migration applied by hand is found to differ from what migrate.mjs would have done (then restore from the backup branch and re-apply by script).

Waiting on NEON_API_KEY and NEON_PROJECT_ID to release round 7 (listed as the owner's item from director16 to director18, about five days). What broke: the release sat blocked on a key the owner did not want to supply ('key rotation I don't want to do'), while the session held a Neon connector able to take the backup branch and run the same statements. Also wrong in the record: OWNER.md said the block was 'production migration 041'; production was at 030 and 16 files were pending, not 8. The count was never read from production's schema_migrations until release day. Lesson: read the target's state before naming a blocker, and ask the owner for the decision (may I use the connector?) rather than for a key.

md.decisions:
## `dc-r16-production-is-the-test-build-2026-11-10` (2026-11-10)

Release 16 (`e807f07`, integration 24) replaced production. Production is the build the owner tests; no staging app.

- **The owner's word:** production can be replaced because nobody is using it; a staging app at $40 to $50 a month was offered and main declined it.
- **Database:** 16 pending migrations (031, 034 to 047, 050) applied through the Neon connector, the owner's choice. Backup branch `pre-release-e807f07` first, a rehearsal of all 49 statements on `rehearse-release-e807f07`, then one transaction on main. Verified: 46 rows in `schema_migrations`.
- **Release:** `scripts/release.mjs e807f07 --migrate skip --force`. The evening freeze protects lessons in progress; there are none.

**Why:** the release had waited since director16 on a Neon key the owner did not want to hand over. The connector needs no key in the repo or the chat.

**Reverse if:**
- a real family starts using production: a staging app (`scripts/staging.mjs`) before any further release, the freeze honoured again, migrations through `scripts/migrate.mjs` with a key in the secret store;
- a migration applied by hand is found to differ from what `migrate.mjs` would have done: restore from the backup branch and re-apply by script.
md.rejected:
## `rj-release-blocked-on-neon-key` (2026-11-10)

The tried approach: waiting on `NEON_API_KEY` and `NEON_PROJECT_ID` to release round 7, listed as the owner's item from director16 to director18.

**What broke:**
- The release sat blocked for about five days on a key the owner did not want to supply, while the session held a Neon connector able to take the backup branch and run the same statements.
- The record was wrong: OWNER.md said the block was "production migration 041". Production was at 030, and 16 files were pending. Nobody had read production's `schema_migrations` until release day.

**Lesson:** read the target's state before naming a blocker, and ask the owner for the decision (may I use the connector?) rather than for a key.
